note: Prices are public list prices looked up on the date above (USD). Usage per user is an assumption written below, not measured. Impact scores are judgments on a 0–10 scale (0 = no improvement over today's free setup, 10 = removes the gap completely). Re-check prices before buying.

usage.app_download_note: The app is one page (about 1.9 MB compressed). Since v210 it is downloaded once per release, not on every launch (service worker answers from cache; version.json triggers the update).
usage.call_min_note: Video-call minutes per active learner per active day (calls are optional; most practice is taps and short turns).

gaps.name: Profe's AI brain
gaps.today: A small AI that runs on the phone (free, offline, makes Spanish mistakes), or Claude with the learner's own Anthropic API key (Profe › Settings › AI brain, re-enabled v255: Haiku / Sonnet / Opus 5.5; the learner pays Anthropic directly, no cost to the app).
gaps.gap: Most learners have no Claude key, so the strongest tutor is unavailable; the on-device model is slow and weaker at grammar.
gaps.driver: per AI reply: input + output tokens

tiers.name: Claude Haiku 5.5 (API, through your own server)
tiers.unit: $0.10 / M input tokens, $0.50 / M output; cached input 0.1×

tiers.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
tiers.unit: $2 / M input, $10 / M output; cached input $0.10

tiers.name: Claude Opus 5.5

gaps.name: Speech recognition
gaps.today: The phone's free Google recogniser (Android SpeechRecognizer).
gaps.gap: No control over accuracy; on the S24 every first start fails with error 11 and is retried; can't tune for learners' accents or for mixed English/Spanish.

tiers.name: Deepgram Nova-3 Multilingual (streaming)

gaps.name: Pronunciation feedback
gaps.today: Only a pass/fail word match from the phone recogniser.
gaps.gap: No sound-by-sound scoring (pero/perro, stress), so pronunciation can't really be taught or graded.

gaps.gap: Robotic or missing voices; learners hear different accents on different phones.

gaps.gap: Changing or losing the phone loses all progress; no way to know who your users are or to sell subscriptions.

gaps.name: Hosting, AI key server and app store
gaps.today: GitHub Pages for the web app; the APK is installed by hand from GitHub Releases. The app downloads only when a new version is released (about 1.9 MB), not on every launch, which keeps GitHub Pages under its 100 GB a month bandwidth guideline at launch scale.
gaps.gap: No server to keep a shared AI key secret; no Play Store listing, automatic updates or payments.
gaps.driver: flat plans + requests; store fee is a share of sales

tiers.name: Cloudflare Pages (free) + Workers Paid for the AI proxy + Play Console
tiers.unit: $5 / month incl. 10 M requests, $0.30 / M after; Play Console $25 once

tiers.name: Same + Cloudflare Pro plan (security, analytics)
Same + Cloudflare Business plan (SLA, priority support)

gaps.name: Profe's video-call face
gaps.today: An original animated character drawn on the phone in code (6 looks): lip sync from the phone's voice, blinking, gaze, smiles and nods. Free, offline, nothing sent anywhere.
gaps.gap: It looks like a stylised drawing, not a lifelike 3D or photoreal tutor like Praktika's; lip sync is only as exact as the word timing the phone's voice reports.
gaps.driver: per video-call minute (streamed avatars) or one-off (characters drawn on the phone)

tiers.name: Licensed 3D characters drawn on the phone (three.js + TalkingHead, MIT)
tiers.unit: ≈$600 one-off: 6 rigged characters with ARKit face shapes at ~$50–150 each + fitting (estimate); +5–10 MB download; still free per minute

tiers.name: Simli streamed face (we keep our own voice and AI)
tiers.unit: $0.05 / call minute, pay as you go

tiers.name: HeyGen LiveAvatar photoreal 1080p (or Tavus, $0.37/min with its own AI)

revenue_note: Selling subscriptions through Google Play costs 15% of subscription revenue (10% service + 5% billing in the US, UK and EEA). That's a share of sales, not a service cost, so it isn't in the totals.
hybrid_note: Biggest saving: keep the phone's free recogniser for commands and conversation, and send only graded speaking answers (about 1 minute a day) to a paid recogniser. That cuts the speech-recognition line by about 80% in every scenario.
